plan.scaleRationale: This is a deliberately expansive single-storey waterfront estate: approximately 390 m² of enclosed principal accommodation plus a substantial sheltered ocean terrace, arrival court, pool surround and detached open-air lounge. The low, spread composition suits a completely flat Saint Lucia oceanfront property, keeps every major room directly connected to exterior living, and invests the $25 million ambition in generous spans, deep shade, crafted material contrast and a complete arrival-to-water sequence rather than unnecessary storeys.
plan.arrivalAndCirculation: Arrival is assumed from the landward south side. A limestone approach court leads to a recessed bronze front door beneath a dedicated canopy. The entrance opens directly into the tall central living salon, with bedroom wings branching west and east. The oceanward axis continues through broad glazed openings to a shaded terrace, pool court and a detached open elliptical ocean lounge pavilion.
plan.volumeHierarchy: The double-height central salon is the unmistakable primary volume. Two lower, broad bedroom/service wings extend laterally from it as quiet subordinate bars. The entrance canopy, ocean terrace canopy and pavilion read as lighter outdoor structures, creating a clear progression from protected landward arrival to open seaward living.
plan.relationshipsAndViews: The central salon is oriented toward the assumed ocean outlook to the north, with three separate framed glazed bays rather than an indiscriminate glass curtain. Its terrace is immediately beyond, shaded by a deep flat canopy and structured by timber posts. The lateral wings retain comparatively solid, private external edges while their inner walls connect back to the central living volume. The pool court and pavilion extend the same central axis without claiming a surveyed shoreline.
plan.roofFacadeAndMaterials: A family of thin, deep flat roofs unifies the low wings, taller salon, entry threshold and terrace canopy. Limestone ground planes and coping establish a durable base palette; ivory walls provide calm tropical mass; bronze doors and slatted screens add depth; timber posts and pavilion furniture soften the ocean-facing outdoor rooms. Material selections express coastal character only and are not corrosion, waterproofing, hurricane, drainage or thermal-performance certifications.

plan.scaleRationale: The explicit request is for a Caribbean beach-house mansion with a US$10M value context. That value label is treated as an ambition for a substantial, carefully composed residence—not as an area or cost formula. This design therefore uses a single-level, approximately 290 m² enclosed main residence plus a large shaded terrace, pool court, arrival forecourt, and detached open lounge pavilion. A one-level arrangement is an intentional accessibility and indoor-outdoor-living response to the assumed beachfront setting, not a reduced programme. Assumptions: the sea/view lies south, the landward arrival is north, the climate is hot-humid, and the site is presently represented as a flat Y=0 plane because generated terrain is not available.
plan.arrivalAndCirculation: Arrival is from the assumed north/landward side across a limestone approach plate to a recessed solid front door under a post-supported canopy. The entry opens into the primary living hall. The private west wing and the compact east service wing connect directly to the hall through shared enclosure walls with actual internal door openings. Broad glazed southern bays lead from the living hall to a continuous pool terrace. The outdoor kitchen sits at the terrace’s eastern end, separated from the pool edge by a clear dry circulation band. The house is single-level, so no stair or upper-level access is required.
plan.volumeHierarchy: Primary volume: living hall centred at [0, 0.1, 0], 14 m wide by 10 m deep, with a 3.2 m enclosure height and broad south-facing glazed bays. Secondary private volume: west wing centred at [-12, 0.1, 1], 10 m by 8 m, visually subordinate beneath a limestone hip roof. Secondary service volume: east wing centred at [10, 0.1, 2], 6 m by 6 m, beneath a lower flat roof. A 18 m by 8 m south terrace begins directly at the living-room threshold. The pool is aligned parallel to the southern view, while the small open elliptical pavilion is set to the pool’s east as a separate sunset lounge.
plan.relationshipsAndViews: The plan assumes south-facing sea views and north-side arrival; these directions are conceptual and not survey data. The living hall is the view-facing centre, with glazed southern bays opening directly to the terrace. The private wing is set westward for separation from the entrance and active outdoor-kitchen zone. The service wing is eastward, adjacent to the outdoor kitchen and away from the pavilion lounge. The pool is rectangular and fully bounded by a modeled basin perimeter; it is not represented as an infinity-edge or hydraulically equipped pool.
plan.roofFacadeAndMaterials: A restrained Caribbean-contemporary palette combines ivory enclosure walls, limestone roof and pool-basin elements, bronze-framed glazed openings, and timber outdoor furnishings. The main hall has a deep flat roof with a 0.5 m perimeter overhang for shade. The private wing is deliberately lower and finished with a hip roof, giving the residence a clear central-to-secondary silhouette. Facade rhythm uses three independent broad glazed south bays across the living hall, smaller shaded openings to the side volumes, solid side returns, and a deeply sheltered entrance rather than an undifferentiated glass box.
